subtitle: What a prefix does to a verb, and telling it again afterwards
words.intro: German has a little word that turns any action into a mistake: *ver-*. You *schreiben*, and then you *verschreiben dich*. You *rechnen*, and you *verrechnen dich*. Learn that, and you can explain how you came to own a wardrobe.

grammar[0].fact: The prefix tells you the story: *ver-* went wrong, *er-* got there in the end, *ent-* took something away. So if you’ve never seen *entkalken*, you can still work out that the machine had *Kalk*, and now it hasn’t. German coffee machines do beg for this, at length, on a display.

grammar[1].fact: When you report what someone said last week, *gestern* becomes *am Vortag* and *morgen* becomes *tags darauf*. Newspapers do this automatically, and so does Frau Huber. *Hier* turns into *dort*, and it can even become *dortig*. Nobody writes it with any pleasure.

document.intro: A real title page. In 1822, a professor’s books were sold from his home in Braunschweig. It’s all one sentence, and all very polite. Look at *weil.*, short for *weiland*, which means *late*, and at the end: *auktionsmäßig verkauft werden sollen*.
document.fact: Johann Joachim Eschenburg was a well-known scholar and an early translator of Shakespeare into German. Printed lists like this were the online auctions of their day: scholars across the country would send in their bids by post.

reading.intro: Max has seen an old wardrobe at an online auction. He wanted to bid 12.00 euros. Paula, a joiner in the Hofstraße, is looking at his screen. She has been told that the wardrobe arrives today. It’s two metres forty high, and Max lives on the fourth floor.
reading.photos[0].caption: Eine alte Hobelbank: Sie hat schon viele Schränke überlebt.
reading.fact: A German joiner trained for years and may have passed a master’s exam, the *Meisterprüfung*. In some crafts, you still need that to open your own business. Young joiners have a tradition called the *Walz*: they travel on foot for years in a black uniform, and they aren’t allowed within 50 km of home.
